title: Rhai policy evaluation for Ravel 2.0.0
intro: How Ravel 2.0.0 evaluates a Rhai owner policy: a separate policy worker computes, and the Ravel CLI performs every host capability. An LLM call is a harness run of Claude Code or Codex, which signs in with the owner's own sign-in. Graph views start at the dark node labelled Start here, and numbered edge labels give the order of steps. Sequences start at their first message, and the state view starts at its initial pseudo-state. The specification docs/specs/policy-evaluation.md is the authority for every rule drawn here.

discussion.title: LLM calls through a harness run
discussion.status: Agreed with the owner. A review-design leaf reads the change next
discussion.summary: The owner chose a harness run with no re-entry for every LLM call. The policy runs Claude Code or Codex with ravel::run_harness, and the harness uses the owner's own sign-in. ravel::llm, the endpoints settings key, the LLM budgets and Rig are removed. The schema check stays as the data helper ravel::json_check. The owner rejected a nested start-session and a nested-session host call.

updatedDiagrams.summary: Removed the LLM adapter and the LLM endpoints. The harness run now reaches the model service with the owner's own sign-in.
The LLM-assisted selection now asks Claude Code through ravel::run_harness, then parses and checks the answer in the worker.
Replaced llm_budget_exhausted with harness_budget_exhausted among the bounds that end the evaluation.
Removed the branch that drops a Rig request. An LLM call stops as a harness run.
Added the rejected nested start-session, which shows the process group that the outer stop cannot reach.

diagrams.title: The CLI acts and the worker computes
diagrams.caption: Two processes during evaluation. Only the Ravel CLI reads files and the environment and launches jobs. A reader thread does its filesystem work, so the runtime keeps watching the deadline. The worker runs the Rhai script and asks for each host capability over fd 3. Ravel holds no model credential: a harness run reaches the model service with the owner's own sign-in. The launch after the reap is in the sequence view.

diagrams.title: One LLM-assisted selection
diagrams.caption: A policy imports one module, asks Claude Code one question through a harness run and selects from the answer. The worker parses the answer with json_parse and checks its shape with json_check. The run and then the worker are reaped before the managed process launches.

diagrams.title: Evaluation states
diagrams.caption: Every refusal happens before the launch. A host call returns to the script as data, including its failures. A rendered state view is not a model check.

diagrams.title: Data or the end of the evaluation
diagrams.caption: The script decides about every operational outcome, including a failed LLM call. The host alone decides about bounds, and the script cannot catch that decision.

diagrams.title: A deadline or a signal stops everything
diagrams.caption: The worker holds no external resource, so the CLI kills it after it stops the host work. The CLI does not wait for a read in progress. An LLM call stops as any harness run. A signal that the CLI consumed wins over the deadline at the final read of the latch. A model service may still finish a request that it accepted.

diagrams.title: Which policy file Ravel evaluates
diagrams.caption: policy.rhai wins when both files exist, so a 1.1.0 session can keep policy.ts during the local upgrade. A lone policy.ts refuses with the migration remedy. start-session inside a harness run refuses first.

diagrams.title: Rejected: a nested start-session
diagrams.caption: REJECTED. A harness run whose program is ravel would select again in a second Ravel CLI, with budgets of its own. Runner 1 stops only the group of its run. Managed process 2 has a group of its own, and both levels use a kill-grace of 5 s, so an outer KILL can leave claude running. The owner chose a harness run with no re-entry instead.
